qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Local route density in cash-in-transit (CIT) and ATM logistics provides scale economies, but sub-hurdle ROIC (~8-9%) and structural secular substitution from digital/contactless payments severely constrain pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Loomis benefits from route density in cash logistics, but multi-cycle ROIC (8-9%) sits well below the 12% threshold and secular decline in cash usage gives banking and retail customers high bargaining power.
qualitative.evidence: Normalized ROIC hovers around 8.4% with 3-year incremental ROIIC around 5.7%, well below the 12% hurdle. Cash handling operates in a structurally contracting volume environment across Europe and the Nordics due to contactless and mobile payments, eroding pricing leverage.
